## Project Overview
This repository is Express, a fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for Node.js [Readme.md:1-9].  
It is a Node.js module distributed through the npm registry for use in server-side applications [Readme.md:50-70].  
The package metadata identifies the module as express version 5.2.1 and specifies a Node.js engine requirement of >= 18 [package.json].  
Typical usage creates an application by importing express, defining routes, and listening on a port (the example listens on 3000) [Readme.md:10-49].  
The core application factory is defined in lib/express.js via createApplication, which mixes in prototypes and initializes the app instance [lib/express.js:36-56].  
Express exposes Router and built-in middleware helpers (json, raw, static, text, urlencoded) as part of its public API [test/exports.js:8-35].  
Key dependencies used by the framework include accepts, body-parser, content-disposition, content-type, cookie, debug, serve-static, and others listed in package.json [package.json].  
The repository includes runnable examples and a comprehensive changelog to illustrate features and track changes over time [examples/README.md:1-29][History.md:1-2].  

## Setup / Installation
Node.js 18 or higher is required to use this project and its packages [Readme.md:50-70][package.json].  
Install the express package into a project using npm with npm install express [Readme.md:50-70].  
To explore this repository’s examples locally, clone the repo, install dependencies with npm install, and run an example with node examples/content-negotiation [Readme.md:129-148].  
This repository configures npm behavior via an .npmrc that disables package-lock, sets a minimum release age, ignores scripts, and disallows installing from git [/.npmrc].  
Linting is configured for an ES2022 and Node environment with rules defined in .eslintrc.yml [/.eslintrc.yml].  
The .gitignore excludes common Node.js artifacts such as node_modules, npm and Yarn lockfiles, logs, coverage outputs, and benchmarking graphs [/.gitignore].  

## Running Locally
This repository is a library and the provided package.json script entries show testing and linting but do not show start or build scripts [package.json].  
For a quick hands-on app, the README demonstrates generating an application with express-generator and starting it with npm start [Readme.md:89-118].  
The quick-start code example listens on http://localhost:3000 and logs that the server is running [Readme.md:10-49].  
To run this repository’s examples, clone the repo, install dependencies, and execute a specific example with node examples/<name> (e.g., node examples/content-negotiation) [Readme.md:129-148].  
For local development against the repo, install dependencies and run the test suite with npm install followed by npm test [Readme.md:163-176].  

## Project Structure
Core framework code lives under lib/, including the application initializer in lib/express.js (createApplication), error logging and safe view rendering helpers in lib/application.js, request property helpers in lib/request.js, response helpers like sendfile and JSON stringification in lib/response.js, utility functions such as acceptParams and ETag generation in lib/utils.js, and a view loader/resolver in lib/view.js [lib/express.js:36-56][lib/application.js:615-631][lib/request.js:521-527][lib/response.js:921-1009][lib/response.js:1023-1047][lib/utils.js:89-120][lib/utils.js:249-257][lib/view.js:52-95].  
The examples/ directory contains many runnable samples (e.g., auth, content-negotiation, cookies, multi-router, mvc, static-files) that demonstrate common patterns and features [examples/README.md:1-29].  
Tests are organized under test/ with both unit and acceptance tests, and the npm test script targets test/ and test/acceptance/ [package.json].  
The test runner preloads a support environment module at test/support/env via the mocha --require flag configured in the scripts [package.json].  
Release notes and historical changes are recorded in History.md [History.md:1-2].  

## Testing
Install dependencies with npm install and run the full test suite with npm test [Readme.md:163-176].  
The package.json defines scripts for several test workflows: test (mocha), test-ci (nyc coverage with lcov and text reporters), test-cov (nyc HTML and text), and test-tap (mocha with tap reporter) [package.json].  
Mocha is the test framework, nyc is used for code coverage, and supertest is included for HTTP assertions in tests [package.json].  
The test command targets test/ and test/acceptance/ and requires test/support/env before running, as configured in the scripts [package.json].  
Acceptance tests demonstrate HTTP behaviors against small Express apps (for example, asserting “Hello World” and a 404 on unknown routes) [test/acceptance/hello-world.js:7-11][test/acceptance/hello-world.js:15-19].  
Unit tests validate the public API surface, such as exposure of Router and middleware helpers on the express export [test/exports.js:8-35].  
If any additional test setup exists beyond test/support/env, it is not shown in the provided evidence [package.json].
